findings.declaration: EndKit19.Endo.mul_val / Endo.one_val / Endo.inv_val / Pts.mul_val / Pts.one_val / Pts.inv_val
findings.excerpt: theorem Endo.mul_val (u v : Endo G) : (u * v).val = G.mul f u.val v.val := rfl
findings.problem: `Endo.val_mk` and `Pts.val_mk` are `@[scoped simp]`. The `val` lemmas for `*`, `1` and `⁻¹` are not, even though they are the matching projection lemmas for the group structure. So `simp` cannot push `.val` through products. Terms such as `(Pts.mk G P * Pts.mk G Q).val` stay stuck, even though `val_mk` is simp. The proofs work around this with `show`, `rfl` or hand-written `Pts.ext`/`congrArg Pts.val` steps. Examples are `isHom_one`, `isHom_inv` (`... mul_inv]; rfl`) and the final `rfl` in `lin_mem_relSubgroup`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `Endo.mul_val`, `Endo.one_val`, `Endo.inv_val`, `Pts.mul_val`, `Pts.one_val` and `Pts.inv_val` as `@[scoped simp]`, as is already done for `val_mk` and `compE_val_coe`. Each right-hand side is built from `G.mul`, `G.one` and `G.inv` applied to `.val` of smaller terms, so a rewrite cannot loop. Together with `val_mk` this gives the normal form `G.mul t P Q` on `SchemeHomOver`. Some proofs could then become a plain `simp`, and the `show`/`rfl` coercions could go.
findings.benefit: Users of the `Endo`/`Pts` type synonyms get one canonical simp normal form. Proofs about `IsHom`, `ev` and `lin` no longer need manual `show`/`rfl` to move between `Pts`/`Endo` and `SchemeHomOver`.

findings.excerpt: theorem bcHom_val_coe (u : Endo G) : (bcHom ι G u).val.1 = NoethBC20.bcEndo ι u.val.1 u.val.2 := rfl
findings.problem: This is the projection lemma for `bcHom`, in the same style as `compE_val_coe`, `idE_val_coe`, `fstPt_coe` and `pushG_coe`, which are all scoped simp. It is not tagged simp. `simp` therefore cannot unfold `(bcHom ι G u).val.1`. It also cannot reach the existing simp lemmas `NoethBC20.bcEndo_fst` and `bcEndo_snd` on terms like `(bcHom ι G u).val.1 ≫ pullback.fst f ι`. The proof of `bcHom_eq_of_fst_comp_eq` calls `rw [bcHom_val_coe, bcHom_val_coe]` by hand before rewriting with the `bcEndo` lemmas.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[scoped simp]` to `bcHom_val_coe`. The right-hand side `bcEndo ι u.val.1 u.val.2` is a different head symbol that does not mention `bcHom`, so there is no cycle. `bcEndo_fst` and `bcEndo_snd` then fire afterwards, and the manual `rw [bcHom_val_coe, ...]` steps can be absorbed into `simp`.
findings.benefit: The simp set for the base-change endomorphism `bcHom` would be complete and consistent with the neighbouring coe lemmas. Goals about `bcHom` compositions would reduce through `bcEndo_fst`/`bcEndo_snd` without manual unfolding.
